syllabus.head: Semiconductor Materials & Properties
syllabus.text: Group-IV materials, covalent bonds, basic energy band concepts in materials (valence band, conduction band, forbidden energy gap).

Intrinsic and extrinsic semiconductors, donor and acceptor impurities, law of mass action (n ·p = n<sub>i</sub><sup>2</sup>), carrier transport: drift current, diffusion current, mobility (μ), conductivity of semiconductors (σ= q(nμ<sub>n</sub> + pμ<sub>p</sub>)), and concept of Fermi level.

syllabus.head: Junction Diode
syllabus.text: P-N junction formation, depletion layer, built-in barrier potential, forward and reverse bias terminal behavior, V-I characteristics, Shockley diode equation, static resistance (R<sub>dc</sub>) and dynamic resistance (r<sub>ac</sub>), diode transition and diffusion capacitances.

syllabus.head: Special Diodes
syllabus.text: Light Emitting Diode (LED: materials, bandgap, emission wavelength λ= hc/E<sub>g</sub>), Varactor diode, Photodiode, Schottky barrier diode, and Tunnel diode (operating principles, energy band diagrams, and characteristic curves).

parts.text: With the help of an energy band diagram, explain the concept of free electrons and holes in an intrinsic semiconductor at room temperature (300 K).
Define intrinsic and extrinsic semiconductors. Explain donor and acceptor impurities in semiconductor materials.
Explain the energy band diagrams for a conductor, semiconductor, and insulator.
Give the classification of semiconductors with suitable examples and diagrams. Explain the concept of Fermi level in intrinsic, N-type, and P-type semiconductors with diagrams and equations.
Define the following parameters: (i) Drift current, (ii) Diffusion current, (iii) Mobility (μ), (iv) Fermi level, (v) Forbidden energy gap.
What is the Law of Mass Action for semiconductors? Write the mass action equation for N-type and P-type semiconductors and explain its physical significance.
Explain the forward and reverse bias characteristics of a P-N junction diode with a circuit diagram.
Define the terms static resistance (R<sub>dc</sub> = V/I) and dynamic resistance (r<sub>ac</sub> = ΔV / ΔI).
Briefly explain the construction and working of a Light Emitting Diode (LED).
Explain the working principle and V-I characteristics of a Tunnel diode and a Schottky diode with the help of neat sketches.

An intrinsic Silicon sample is doped with phosphorus to 10<sup>17</sup> cm<sup>-3</sup> at 300 K. Calculate the majority and minority carrier concentrations, and the electrical conductivity (σ) of the extrinsic Si sample. Take n<sub>i</sub> = 1.5 ×10<sup>10</sup> cm<sup>-3</sup>, electron mobility μ<sub>n</sub> = 1300 cm<sup>2</sup>/V·s, and hole mobility μ<sub>p</sub> = 500 cm<sup>2</sup>/V·s.

Find the conductivity of silicon: (i) In intrinsic condition at 300 K, (ii) With donor impurity of 1 in 10<sup>8</sup> Si atoms, and (iii) With acceptor impurity of 1 in 5 ×10<sup>7</sup> Si atoms. Given: n<sub>i</sub> = 1.5 ×10<sup>10</sup> cm<sup>-3</sup>, μ<sub>n</sub> = 1300 cm<sup>2</sup>/V·s, μ<sub>p</sub> = 500 cm<sup>2</sup>/V·s, and total Si atoms per cm<sup>3</sup> = 5 ×10<sup>22</sup>.

A Silicon diode has a reverse saturation current I<sub>s</sub> = 2 nA at room temperature (T = 300 K). Determine the forward diode current at an applied forward bias voltage of 0.6 V. Take the diode ideality factor η= 2 and thermal voltage V<sub>T</sub> = 26 mV.
The reverse saturation current of a silicon P-N junction diode is 10 μA. Calculate the diode current for a forward bias voltage of 0.6 V at 25°C.

Determine the wavelength (λ) of light emitted from an LED made of a GaAsP semiconductor whose forbidden energy gap is E<sub>g</sub> = 1.875 eV. Mention the color of the emitted light (Take Planck's constant h = 6.6 ×10<sup>-34</sup> J·s). Also explain the concept of energy band diagrams in materials.

labs.title: 3D Semiconductor Band Structure & Carrier Drift-Diffusion Simulator
points: Physical 3D Assets:
3D atomic lattice matrix (Diamond cubic Silicon crystal) displaying covalent bonds between Silicon atoms.
Visual energy band level tower displaying the Valence Band, Forbidden Gap (E<sub>g</sub> = 1.12 eV), Conduction Band, and movable Fermi Level (E<sub>F</sub>).
Interactive Controls:
Temperature slider (0 K to 500 K).
Dopant selector: Intrinsic vs. N-Type (Phosphorus/Arsenic pentavalent atoms) vs. P-Type (Boron trivalent atoms).
Doping concentration slider (N<sub>D</sub>, N<sub>A</sub> from 10<sup>14</sup> to 10<sup>19</sup> cm<sup>-3</sup>).
Applied external electric field vector (E⃗).
Real-Time Visual Mechanics:
Thermal Generation: At T > 0 K, thermal agitation breaks covalent bonds; valence electrons break loose and jump across the bandgap into the conduction band, leaving behind mobile positive holes.

Doping & Fermi Level Movement: Adding donor atoms introduces discrete donor energy states ED just below Ec, elevating the Fermi level EF toward the conduction band; acceptor doping introduces EA just above Ev, pulling EF toward the valence band.

Transport Mechanics: Under an electric field, conduction electrons drift opposite to E⃗ while holes drift parallel to E⃗; displays real-time carrier densities (n, p) and computes conductivity σ matching exam numerical algorithms.

labs.title: P-N Junction Depletion Dynamics & Diode V-I Tracer
points: Physical 3D Assets:
Microscopic P-N junction block with transparent casing showing fixed ionized donor cores (⊕) and acceptor cores (⊖), mobile electrons, mobile holes, and a dynamic central depletion region.
Virtual curve tracer workstation connected to an adjustable DC bias power supply.
Interactive Controls:
Bias voltage control slider (-10 V reverse bias to +1.0 V forward bias).
Diode material toggle: Silicon (V<sub>γ</sub>= 0.7 V) vs. Germanium (V<sub>γ</sub>= 0.3 V).
Diode Type Selector: Standard Rectifier Diode vs. Tunnel Diode vs. LED.
Real-Time Visual Mechanics:

Forward Bias: Applied voltage opposes the built-in barrier potential; depletion layer narrows, barrier height collapses, and majority carriers diffuse across the junction, producing exponential forward current.

Reverse Bias: Applied field widens the depletion layer, increasing barrier height; majority current ceases, leaving only thermally generated minority carriers to form a constant nano-ampere reverse saturation current (Is).
Live Display: Synchronously plots the V-I curve, calculating static resistance (Rdc) and dynamic resistance (rac = ηVT/ID) dynamically.

syllabus.head: Diode Applications
syllabus.text: Half-Wave Rectifier (HWR), Full-Wave Rectifiers: Centre-Tapped and Bridge Rectifier (circuit operation, input/output waveforms, average DC current/voltage, RMS current/voltage).
Performance metrics: Ripple factor (γ), Rectification efficiency (η), Form factor, Peak Inverse Voltage (PIV), Transformer Utilization Factor (TUF).
Filters: Shunt capacitor filter (C), ripple factor with filter.
Wave Shaping Circuits: Clipping circuits (positive, negative, biased, combination clippers), Clamping circuits (positive and negative clampers).
Voltage Multipliers: Voltage doubler, voltage tripler, and voltage quadrupler circuits.

syllabus.head: Breakdown Mechanisms in Diodes
syllabus.text: Avalanche breakdown vs. Zener breakdown (carrier multiplication, impact ionization vs. quantum tunneling, electric field intensity, temperature coefficient).

syllabus.head: Zener Diode as Voltage Regulator
syllabus.text: Breakdown voltage (V<sub>Z</sub>), Zener resistance (R<sub>Z</sub>), knee current (I<sub>ZK</sub>), maximum current (I<sub>ZM</sub>), shunt voltage regulator circuit analysis with variable input voltage (line regulation) and variable load resistance (load regulation).

parts.text: With a neat circuit diagram and input/output waveforms, explain the working of a Full-Wave Bridge Rectifier. Derive the mathematical expression for its rectification efficiency (η= 81.2%).
Explain the working of a full-wave Centre-Tap rectifier with a circuit diagram. Calculate the Ripple factor (γ= 0.482) and Rectification Efficiency for a centre-tapped full-wave rectifier.
Explain the breakdown mechanisms in a P-N junction diode.
Differentiate between Avalanche breakdown and Zener breakdown with respect to doping concentration, depletion width, electric field intensity, temperature coefficient, and V-I characteristics.
Explain the classification and working of diode Clipper and Clamper circuits.
Draw the circuit diagram of a biased positive clamper circuit and explain its operational mechanism with input/output waveforms.
Explain the working principle and circuit configuration of a voltage tripler circuit using diodes and capacitors.

pyqs.title: Zener Diode as a Shunt Voltage Regulator

parts.text: Explain how a Zener diode maintains a constant output voltage across a load despite variations in input supply voltage (line regulation) and variations in load resistance (load regulation).

For the clipper circuit shown, the input voltage v<sub>i</sub>(t) is a sine wave given by 5sin(100πt) V. The circuit consists of a series resistor R followed by a parallel branch containing a diode in series with a DC reference voltage V = 1 V connected to ground. Determine and sketch the transfer characteristics and exact output voltage waveform (v<sub>o</sub>).

For the clamping network shown (capacitor C = 1 μF, parallel diode in series with a 1.5 V DC source, load resistor R<sub>L</sub> = 100 kΩ, square wave input of frequency f = 1000 Hz and peak ±20 V): (i) Calculate 5τ (5 R<sub>L</sub> C). (ii) Compare 5τ to half the period of the applied input signal (T/2). (iii) Sketch the steady-state output waveform (v<sub>o</sub>).

In a full-wave bridge rectifier, the load resistance is R<sub>L</sub> = 1 kΩ. Each silicon diode has a forward dynamic resistance r<sub>d</sub> = 10 Ω. The voltage across the secondary winding is 220sin(314t) V. Find: (a) Peak value of load current (I<sub>m</sub>), (b) DC average load current (I<sub>dc</sub>), (c) RMS value of load current (I<sub>rms</sub>), (d) Ripple factor (γ), and (e) Rectification efficiency (η).

A full-wave bridge rectifier operates with a 120 V RMS sinusoidal input and a load resistance R<sub>L</sub> = 1 kΩ. If silicon diodes are employed (V<sub>D</sub> = 0.7 V): (i) What is the DC voltage available at the load, (ii) Determine the required PIV rating of each diode, (iii) Find the peak maximum current through each diode during conduction.

pyqs.title: Zener Shunt Regulator Circuit Design & Limits

parts.text: A Zener diode voltage regulator circuit has an input voltage V<sub>in</sub> = 16 V, series resistance R<sub>s</sub> = 1 kΩ, Zener voltage V<sub>Z</sub> = 10 V, and load resistor R<sub>L</sub> = 3 kΩ. Determine the values of load voltage (V<sub>L</sub>), voltage drop across series resistor (V<sub>R</sub>), Zener current (I<sub>Z</sub>), and power dissipated by the Zener diode (P<sub>Z</sub>).

Determine the range of input values of V<sub>i</sub> that will maintain the Zener diode in the "ON" breakdown regulation state for a circuit with series resistor R = 220 Ω, Zener voltage V<sub>Z</sub> = 20 V, maximum Zener current I<sub>ZM</sub> = 60 mA, and load resistor R<sub>L</sub> = 1.2 kΩ.

Design a Zener regulator network to maintain load voltage V<sub>L</sub> = 12 V across a load varying from I<sub>L</sub> = 0 mA to 200 mA from an unregulated input source of 16 V. Determine the required series resistance R<sub>s</sub> and diode rating V<sub>Z</sub>.

A 6 V Zener diode has zero internal resistance and a knee current I<sub>ZK</sub> = 5 mA. Connected across an unregulated supply of 12 V with a series resistor R<sub>s</sub> = 500 Ω, determine the minimum value of load resistance R<sub>L</sub> such that output voltage does not fall below 6 V.

labs.title: Diode Wave-Shaping & Zener Voltage Regulation Workbench
points: Physical 3D Assets:
Function generator outputting variable waveforms (sine, square, triangular), DC reference bias supplies, silicon diodes, precision Zener diode (V<sub>Z</sub> = 10 V), and variable DC input supply.
Interactive Controls:
Circuit Function Mode: Positive/Negative Clipper vs. Clamper vs. Zener Shunt Regulator.
Clipper DC reference voltage slider (-5 V to +5 V).
Unregulated input DC voltage slider (0 V to 30 V).
Load current draw slider (0 mA to 250 mA).
Real-Time Visual Mechanics:
Clipper Mode: Visualizes waveform clipping at threshold level Vref + Vγ; displays transfer characteristic curve (Vo vs. Vi) live.

Clamper Mode: Demonstrates initial capacitor charging through the forward-biased diode during the first negative peak, establishing a permanent DC offset that clamps the signal without altering its peak-to-peak amplitude.

Zener Regulator Mode: Increasing input voltage drives the operating point down the steep reverse breakdown knee; Zener current (IZ) rises dynamically to absorb excess current, clamping load voltage (VL) strictly to VZ = 10 V until current ratings are exceeded.

syllabus.head: Bipolar Junction Transistors (BJT)
syllabus.text: Basic physical construction (NPN and PNP), doping profiles, region widths (emitter, base, collector), transistor action, current components in active mode (I<sub>E</sub> = I<sub>B</sub> + I<sub>C</sub>), and minority carrier leakage currents (I<sub>CBO</sub>, I<sub>CEO</sub>).

syllabus.head: Transistor Configurations
syllabus.text: Common Base (CB), Common Emitter (CE), and Common Collector (CC) configurations, input and output static characteristic curves, active, saturation, and cutoff operational regions.
Current amplification factors: α (CB), β (CE), γ (CC), and mathematical derivations of their inter-relationships (β= α/(1-α), γ= 1+β).

syllabus.head: BJT Biasing Circuits
syllabus.text: Need for biasing, DC load line, operating quiescent point (Q-point), thermal runaway, stability factor (S), Fixed bias circuit, Emitter-stabilized bias, and Voltage Divider (potential divider) bias circuit analysis.

syllabus.head: Transistor Amplifiers
syllabus.text: Graphical dynamic analysis of a CE BJT amplifier, low-frequency small-signal equivalent circuits, hybrid parameter (h-parameter) model (h<sub>ie</sub>, h<sub>re</sub>, h<sub>fe</sub>, h<sub>oe</sub>), and r<sub>e</sub> model.
Derivations for single-stage CE and CC amplifiers: Input resistance (R<sub>i</sub>), Output resistance (R<sub>o</sub>), Current gain (A<sub>i</sub>), and Voltage gain (A<sub>v</sub>).

parts.text: With the help of a construction diagram, explain the flow of various internal current components in a PNP and NPN BJT operating in the active region.
Define current amplification factors α, β, and γ. Derive the mathematical relations between α, β, and γ.
Differentiate between a Bipolar Junction Transistor (BJT) and a Field Effect Transistor (FET/MOSFET).

Draw the circuit diagram and explain the input and output static characteristic curves of an NPN BJT in Common Emitter (CE) configuration. Clearly indicate the Active, Cut-off, and Saturation regions.
Sketch the Common Base (CB) BJT transistor configuration, indicate the polarities of applied external DC bias voltages, and explain its input/output characteristics.
What is transistor biasing? What are the basic requirements of a transistor biasing circuit, and why is stabilization of the Q-point necessary against temperature variations and β changes?
Draw the circuit diagram of a Fixed Bias circuit, determine its Q-point coordinates (I<sub>BQ</sub>, I<sub>CQ</sub>, V<sub>CEQ</sub>), and explain its primary disadvantages.
Explain the circuit arrangement and analytical equations of the Voltage Divider (Potential Divider) bias circuit. Why is it considered the most stable biasing method?

A Common Emitter (CE) BJT amplifier is connected to source resistance R<sub>S</sub> and load resistance R<sub>L</sub>. Using the low-frequency h-parameter equivalent model, derive the expressions for: (i) Current gain (A<sub>i</sub>), (ii) Input resistance (R<sub>i</sub>), (iii) Voltage gain (A<sub>v</sub>), and (iv) Output resistance (R<sub>o</sub>).
Derive the expressions for input impedance, output impedance, current gain, and voltage gain for a Common Emitter BJT configuration using the r<sub>e</sub> small-signal model.

For the self-bias / fixed-bias CE circuit shown (collector supply V<sub>CC</sub> = 12 V, collector resistor R<sub>C</sub> = 3 kΩ, base resistor R<sub>B</sub> = 500 kΩ, emitter resistor R<sub>E</sub> = 700 Ω), determine the base current (I<sub>B</sub>), collector current (I<sub>C</sub>), and collector-to-emitter voltage (V<sub>CE</sub>). Take β= 200 and V<sub>BE</sub> = 0.7 V.

In a CE configuration, current gain is β= 98 and collector-to-emitter leakage current is I<sub>CEO</sub> = 40 μA. If the base current is I<sub>B</sub> = 0.3 mA, calculate the collector current I<sub>C</sub> and emitter current I<sub>E</sub>.
Given α<sub>dc</sub> = 0.997, determine the corresponding value of β<sub>dc</sub>.
A transistor operating with β<sub>dc</sub> = 180 has a collector current I<sub>C</sub> = 2 mA. Find the base current I<sub>B</sub> and emitter current I<sub>E</sub>.

points: Physical 3D Assets:

Variable dual DC power supplies (V<sub>BB</sub>, V<sub>CC</sub>) connected across test terminals.
Interactive Controls:
Transistor Type Toggle: NPN vs. PNP.
Configuration Selector: Common Emitter (CE) vs. Common Base (CB) vs. Common Collector (CC).
Input voltage drive slider (V<sub>BE</sub>) and Output voltage sweep slider (V<sub>CE</sub>).
Real-Time Visual Mechanics:

Active Mode Electron Injection: Shows electrons injected from emitter diffusing across the ultra-thin base; 95--99% pass through base-collector depletion layer into the collector, while 1--5% recombine with holes and exit via base lead.

Input Tab: Traces diode-like I<sub>B</sub> vs. V<sub>BE</sub> curve showing knee voltage at 0.7 V.

labs.title: BJT Biasing Stability & Small-Signal AC Amplifier Bench
points: Physical 3D Assets:

Standard audio-frequency single-stage CE amplifier breadboard featuring transistor, coupling capacitors (C<sub>1</sub>, C<sub>2</sub>), emitter bypass capacitor (C<sub>E</sub>), biasing resistors (R<sub>1</sub>, R<sub>2</sub>, R<sub>C</sub>, R<sub>E</sub>), and load R<sub>L</sub>.
Signal generator injecting a 1 kHz sinusoidal test wave and dual-channel oscilloscope.
Interactive Controls:
Biasing Topology Switch: Fixed Bias vs. Emitter Bias vs. Voltage Divider Bias.
Transistor junction temperature slider (25°C to 125°C).
Small-signal input voltage amplitude slider (1 mV to 50 mV).
Real-Time Visual Mechanics:
DC Load Line Visualization: Plots the load line between VCC and VCC/(RC + RE); positions the operating Q-point (VCEQ, ICQ).

Thermal Stability Test: As temperature rises, β and ICBO increase; Fixed Bias shows the Q-point drifting toward saturation (thermal runaway), whereas Voltage Divider Bias demonstrates negative feedback stabilization holding the Q-point stable.
AC Signal Amplification: Oscilloscope shows the amplified output voltage waveform inverted by 180° relative to input, calculating voltage gain Av = vo / vi live.

syllabus.head: Junction Field Effect Transistor (JFET)
syllabus.text: Physical construction and working of N-channel and P-channel JFETs, channel conductivity, depletion layer profile under reverse bias.

JFET characteristics: Drain static characteristics (I<sub>D</sub> vs. V<sub>DS</sub>), transfer characteristics (I<sub>D</sub> vs. V<sub>GS</sub>), Shockley's equation: I<sub>D</sub> = I<sub>DSS</sub> (1 - V<sub>GS</sub>/V<sub>P</sub>)<sup>2</sup>, pinch-off voltage (V<sub>P</sub>), and maximum drain saturation current (I<sub>DSS</sub>).

JFET operational parameters: Dynamic drain resistance (r<sub>d</sub> = ΔV<sub>DS</sub>/ΔI<sub>D</sub>), transconductance (g<sub>m</sub> = ΔI<sub>D</sub>/ΔV<sub>GS</sub>), amplification factor (μ= r<sub>d</sub> ·g<sub>m</sub>).
JFET Configurations & Biasing: Common Source (CS), Common Drain (CD), Common Gate (CG), fixed bias, self-bias, and voltage-divider bias circuits.

syllabus.head: Metal Oxide Semiconductor FET (MOSFET)
syllabus.text: Depletion-type MOSFET (D-MOSFET) and Enhancement-type MOSFET (E-MOSFET).
Construction, operating principle, inversion layer formation, threshold voltage (V<sub>TH</sub>), drain and transfer characteristics for N-channel and P-channel D-MOSFET and E-MOSFET.

syllabus.head: FET Small-Signal Amplifiers
syllabus.text: Small-signal equivalent model of JFET/MOSFET, analysis of single-stage Common Source (CS) amplifier, phase inversion (180°), derivation of voltage gain (A<sub>v</sub> = -g<sub>m</sub> (r<sub>d</sub> ∥R<sub>D</sub>)), input resistance (R<sub>i</sub>), and output resistance (R<sub>o</sub>).

parts.text: Explain the construction and working of an N-channel JFET with a neat structural diagram.

Define and explain the following JFET parameters in detail: (i) Pinch-off voltage (V<sub>P</sub>), (ii) Maximum saturation drain current (I<sub>DSS</sub>), (iii) Transconductance (g<sub>m</sub>), (iv) Drain resistance (r<sub>d</sub>), and (v) Amplification factor (μ).
Sketch and explain the typical drain characteristics (I<sub>D</sub> vs. V<sub>DS</sub>) and transfer characteristics (I<sub>D</sub> vs. V<sub>GS</sub>) of an N-channel JFET.
Draw the construction diagram of an N-channel Enhancement-type MOSFET and explain its working operation, inversion channel formation, and transfer/drain characteristics.
With the help of a construction diagram, explain the working and characteristics of an N-channel Depletion-type MOSFET. Why can a D-MOSFET operate in both depletion and enhancement modes?
State the important structural, electrical, and operational differences between Bipolar Junction Transistors (BJT) and Field Effect Transistors (FET/MOSFET) in a comparative table.

Draw the circuit diagram of a Common Source (CS) amplifier using an N-channel JFET. Explain the phase relationship between the input and output signals, and derive the expression for its small-signal voltage gain using the AC equivalent model.
Explain the fixed-bias and self-bias configurations of a JFET with circuit diagrams and analytical equations.

The JFET has I<sub>DSS</sub> = 10 mA and pinch-off voltage V<sub>P</sub> = -4 V.

Real-Time Visual Mechanics:
Ohmic Region: At low VDS, channel behaves like a linear resistor; electrons flow freely from source to drain.

Pinch-Off Dynamics: As VDS increases, reverse bias across gate-channel junction becomes larger near the drain end than the source end; depletion boundaries expand asymmetrically into the N-channel, pinching down the conduction path into a narrow constriction.
Saturation (Pinch-Off): Beyond VDS = VGS - VP, depletion regions touch; current saturates at a constant level (ID = IDSS).
Synchronously plots drain family curves (I<sub>D</sub> vs. V<sub>DS</sub>) and transfer curve (I<sub>D</sub> vs. V<sub>GS</sub>).

labs.title: MOSFET Gate Oxide Field Effect & Transconductance Rig
points: Physical 3D Assets:

Volumetric 3D model of an N-channel Enhancement MOSFET: P-type substrate body, two isolated N<sup>+</sup> wells (Source and Drain), thin silicon dioxide (SiO<sub>2</sub>) insulating dielectric layer, and metallic Gate terminal plate.
Interactive Controls:
Gate voltage slider (V<sub>GS</sub> from 0 V to +8 V).
Drain voltage slider (V<sub>DS</sub> from 0 V to +15 V).
Oxide dielectric thickness slider (t<sub>ox</sub>).
Real-Time Visual Mechanics:
Sub-Threshold (VGS < VTH): Positive gate repels holes from the oxide interface, forming a carrier-depleted zone; no current flows (ID = 0).
Channel Inversion (VGS > VTH): High electric field attracts minority electrons toward the SiO2 boundary, forming a conductive N-type surface inversion layer linking Source and Drain.
Conduction: Applying VDS sweeps electrons through the inverted channel; displays real-time electron density and plots square-law saturation characteristics:

units.title: Switching Theory, Logic Design & Operational Amplifiers

syllabus.head: Switching Theory & Logic Design
syllabus.text: Number systems: Decimal, Binary, Octal, and Hexadecimal systems, base conversion methods (integers and fractional numbers).
Boolean algebra: Fundamental postulates, algebraic theorems, De Morgan's theorems.
Logic Gates: Basic gates (AND, OR, NOT), Universal gates (NAND, NOR), Exclusive gates (XOR, XNOR), truth tables, implementation of basic logic functions using NAND/NOR universal gates only.

Minimization of Boolean Functions: Sum of Products (SOP) and Product of Sums (POS) standard forms, minterms and maxterms, Karnaugh Map (K-map) minimization up to 4 variables, grouping rules, and handling "Don't Care" (d) conditions.

syllabus.head: Operational Amplifiers (Op-Amp)
syllabus.text: Concept of ideal operational amplifier, equivalent circuit, block diagram, internal stages.

Ideal Op-Amp parameters: Open-loop voltage gain (A<sub>OL</sub> = ∞), input impedance (R<sub>in</sub> = ∞), output impedance (R<sub>out</sub> = 0), bandwidth (BW = ∞), Common Mode Rejection Ratio (CMRR = ∞), Slew Rate (SR = ∞), and offset voltage (V<sub>os</sub> = 0).
Virtual ground concept and virtual short principle.

Linear Op-Amp Applications: Inverting amplifier, Non-inverting amplifier, Unity-gain buffer (voltage follower), Summing amplifier (adder), and Difference amplifier (subtractor) with circuit diagrams and closed-loop gain derivations.
